title: T-Accounts
description: Visualize how debits and credits affect accounts.
html:
What is a T-account?

A T-account is a simple visual way to show increases and decreases in an account.

The left side is always the debit side and the right side is always the credit side.

Cash
Debit Left Side
Credit Right Side

Important

Debit always means LEFT.

Credit always means RIGHT.

But whether the account increases or decreases depends on the account type.

Example: Receiving cash

Suppose a business receives $5,000 cash from its owner.

Cash is an asset. Assets increase with debits.

Cash
Debit $5,000
Credit —

Example: Paying cash

Now suppose the business pays $1,000 rent.

Cash decreases. Because Cash is an asset, a decrease is recorded with a credit.

Cash
Debit $5,000
Credit $1,000

Ending Cash Balance

$5,000 debit − $1,000 credit = $4,000 debit balance.

Remember

  • Debit = left.
  • Credit = right.
  • Assets normally have debit balances.
  • Liabilities normally have credit balances.
  • Equity normally has a credit balance.
  • Revenue normally has a credit balance.
  • Expenses normally have debit balances.

quiz.prompt: Cash has a $9,000 debit and a $2,500 credit. What is the ending balance?
quiz.explanation: Cash is an asset. $9,000 debit minus $2,500 credit gives a $6,500 debit balance.
